title: Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR
statement: You get an integer array `arr`. For indices `i`, `j` and `k` with `0 <= i < j <= k < arr.length`, let `a` be the bitwise XOR of `arr[i..j-1]` and `b` the bitwise XOR of `arr[j..k]` (both ranges inclusive, so each half holds at least one element). Return how many such triplets `(i, j, k)` have `a == b`.
notes:
## Intuition

If `a == b` then `a ^ b == 0`, and `a ^ b` is just the XOR of the whole range `arr[i..k]`. So a triplet works exactly when `arr[i..k]` XORs to zero, and then **every** split point `j` from `i + 1` to `k` works: that is `k - i` triplets. The brute force tries all `(i, j, k)`; we only need ranges with XOR zero.

With prefix XORs (`prefix` after position `p` is the XOR of the first `p` values), `arr[i..k]` XORs to zero when the prefix at position `i` equals the prefix at position `k + 1`.

## Approach

1. Keep, for each prefix value, `count` (how many positions had it) and `positionSum` (the sum of those positions). Position 0 has prefix 0.
2. For each `k`, fold `arr[k]` into `prefix`; this is the prefix at position `k + 1`.
3. Every earlier position `i` with the same prefix adds `k - i` triplets. Summed over them that is `seen * k - total`, so add it to `triplets`.
4. Record position `k + 1` under `prefix`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [2,3,1,6,7]`. Prefixes at positions 0..5 are `0, 2, 1, 0, 6, 1`.

- `k = 2`: `prefix = 0`, seen once at position 0, add `1·2 - 0 = 2` (triplets `(0,1,2)` and `(0,2,2)`).
- `k = 4`: `prefix = 1`, seen once at position 2, add `1·4 - 2 = 2` (triplets `(2,3,4)` and `(2,4,4)`).
- Every other `k` meets a new prefix and adds 0.

`triplets = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time map work per element.
- Space: O(n) for the two maps.

## Pitfalls

- `j` may equal `k`, so `b` can be one element; a range of length `L` gives `L - 1` triplets, not `L - 2`.
- Seed the maps with prefix 0 at position 0, or ranges starting at index 0 are missed.
- Store position `k + 1` (the prefix's position), not `k`, so `seen * k - total` counts `k - i` exactly.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | XOR of `arr[0..k]`, the prefix at position `k + 1` |
| `count` | prefix value → how many positions so far had it |
| `positionSum` | prefix value → sum of those positions |
| `seen`, `total` | the two map entries for the current `prefix` |
| `triplets` | answer so far |

narration.2: Prefix 0 has been seen once, at position 0 (before any element).
narration.3: Track the sum of positions for each prefix value, starting with position 0.
narration.6: Treat each index k as the right end of a range.
narration.7: Fold arr[k] in, giving the XOR of the first k + 1 values.
narration.8: How many earlier positions i had this same prefix, so that arr[i..k] XORs to zero?
narration.9: The sum of those positions i.
narration.10: Each such i allows k - i split points j; adding them all is seen * k - total.
narration.11: Record that position k + 1 has this prefix.
narration.12: Add position k + 1 to the sum for this prefix.
narration.14: Every zero-XOR range has been counted with all its split points.
